record.task: Fix req-shield review findings: core rejection unlock guard, reactor scheduler-rejection lock leak, fail-fast name lookup for aspect executor/scheduler/scope beans, non-vacuous tests
record.result: All 4 fixed; 355 tests, ktlint, jacoco pass; every new test fails under a targeted mutation
learnings: When a Reactor write chain has two subscribeOn operators (one at the call site, one inside a helper), moving the lock-release doFinally after the inner subscribeOn is not enough: the outer one is rejected first and never subscribes the inner chain; remove the redundant outer subscribeOn too.

To make a Spring component fail fast on a wrong-typed optional named bean, resolve it in setBeanFactory with containsBean(name) then getBean(name, T): a bean of another type throws BeanNotOfRequiredTypeException at refresh, and a bean declared as Any that returns a T still works.
Inside a MockK answers { } lambda the name value refers to the answer scope's own member, not the test's property, so build the returned object outside the lambda.

[req-shield] 2026-09-25_2227 req-shield core: handle executor rejection in ReqShield background cache write/refresh :: CompletableFuture.runAsync(task, executor) throws RejectedExecutionException synchronously on the caller thread (from Executor.execute) when a bounded pool is full or shut down, so any lock the task would release in its finally leaks; catch it at the call site and release the lock there.

[req-shield] 2026-09-25_2240 req-shield: fix DST skew in nowToEpochTime and document WebFlux adapter Mono-only limitation :: LocalDateTime.now().atZone(ZoneId.systemDefault()).toInstant() picks the earlier offset during a DST fall-back overlap, so for that hour it returns epoch millis one hour behind System.currentTimeMillis; compute 'now' in epoch millis with System.currentTimeMillis() or Instant.now(), never via LocalDateTime. | A Spring AOP @Around advice that returns a lazy Mono silently does nothing on a void (Unit) method: the proxy discards the return value, nothing subscribes, and the target method body never runs; on other non-Mono return types the caller gets a ClassCastException.

[req-shield] 2026-09-26_2133 req-shield pre-release: stop Spring adapters from registering executor/scheduler/coroutine-scope beans; aspects resolve an optional app bean by name, else own a default :: Spring Boot's applicationTaskExecutor is @ConditionalOnMissingBean(Executor). A library auto-configuration that registers any Executor bean silently removes it in apps without Spring MVC (WebMvcAutoConfiguration declares after=TaskExecutionAutoConfiguration, which otherwise orders Boot's executor first), so @Async falls back to an unbounded SimpleAsyncTaskExecutor. Test it with a Boot app that excludes WebMvcAutoConfiguration. | A library @Bean with a fixed name clashes with an application bean of the same name under Spring Boot (bean overriding disallowed -> BeanDefinitionOverrideException), so don't register it: look up the optional application bean by name and fall back to a default the component owns; reproduce the clash in plain-Spring tests with context.setAllowBeanDefinitionOverriding(false). | Spring 6.1+ SimpleKeyGenerator and MethodBasedEvaluationContext drop the trailing Continuation of a suspend function themselves. Detect 6.1 by the presence of org.springframework.aop.framework.CoroutinesUtils, not SpringVersion.getVersion(), which is null in shaded jars and then causes the real last argument to be dropped from cache keys. | kotlinx.coroutines debug mode (on under -ea in Gradle tests) appends ' @coroutine#N' to thread names, so thread-name assertions inside coroutines must use startsWith. | Running two Gradle builds on the same project at once makes test tasks fail with 'Could not write XML test results' - a false failure; run builds sequentially before trusting results.

[req-shield] 2026-09-26_2133_2 Review req-shield changes: Spring adapters resolve optional named executor/scheduler/scope beans; reactor cancel releases lock; core handles executor rejection :: In Reactor, a doFinally placed before subscribeOn(scheduler) never runs when the scheduler rejects the task (disposed or saturated): MonoSubscribeOn sends onError without subscribing upstream, so a lock release there leaks; put the release after subscribeOn or handle RejectedExecutionException. | @Qualifier("x") ObjectProvider<T>.getIfAvailable filters candidates by type before applying the qualifier, so a bean named x whose declared type is not T is silently ignored and the fallback is used; resolve by name with beanFactory.getBean(name, T) to fail loudly.
